lawyer:
Mr. Hasan Foiz Siddiquie, Advocate for the Petitioner.
None, For the opposite party.
parties:
Basharatullah ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Managing Committee for New Academy and another ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Syed Amirul Islam, J: This Rule at the instance of the plaintiff is directed against the judgment and decree dated 1.2.1993 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Jhenaidah in Title Appeal No. 80 of 1990 reversing the judgment and decree dated 6.3.1990 passed by the Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Jhenaidah in Title Suit No. 464 of 1986. 

 4. The learned trial court decreed the suit and being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree of the trial court dated 6.3.90, the defendant preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge, Jessore which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge, Jhenidah vide his judgment and decree dated 1.2.93 whereby he reversed the judgment of the trial court and dismissed the suit. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 01.2.93 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Jessore in Title Appeal No. 80 of 1990 the plaintiff obtained the present Rule. 

 5. On a perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that the learned appellate court below dismissed the suit on the ground that the suit is not maintainable as framed and for want of any consequential relief and as such the same was hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The learned appellate court below on this legal ground dismissed the suit although he found that the plaintiff petitioner was not given any personal hearing before the order of dismissal was passed by the Managing Committee of the School and thereby he concurred with the finding of the trial court that the order of dismissal was illegal and violative of the principle of natural justice. On a perusal of the trial court's judgment it appears that the learned trial court found that the plaintiff petitioner was not given personal hearing before passing the dismissal order. The learned trial court thereafter decreed the suit on the basis of exhibit A(10) on the finding that the resolution dated 5.11.85 was not approved by the appeal and arbitration committee of the Board and the Board directed the school authority to observe the conduct of the plaintiff for 6 months and thereafter to send a report to the appeal and Arbitration Committee. The learned trial Court arrived at a finding that since in pursuance of the order of appeal and arbitration committee the plaintiff petitioner was reinstated in the service the resolution dated 5.11.85 lost its force and died its natural death and if the Managing Committee wanted to dismiss the plaintiff from service of the school they were to initiate a fresh disciplinary proceeding against the plaintiff in accordance with the regulation of the Board but in the instant case the Managing Committee instead of complying with the provision as laid down in the Rules of the Board they have fallen back to their resolution dated 5.11.85 and dismissed the plaintiff illegally. 

 6. Mr. Hasan Foiz Siddique, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner, firstly submits that there are contradictory decisions of the High Court Division on the point as to whether a suit for simple declaration in a service matter without any prayer for consequential relief is maintainable or not and relying on the decision reported in 11 B.L.D. 528, he submits that the instant suit is maintainable without any prayer for consequential relief. When his attention was drawn to the decision of the Appellate Division as pronounced in Special Leave to Appeal No. 229 of 1983 he found it difficult to support his submission and frankly conceded that in view of the decision of the Appellate Division in the Special Leave to Appeal No. 229 of 1983 it is now well settled that a suit for simple declaration without prayer for consequential relief enforcing the declaratory decree is not maintainable and to overcome that difficulty he filed an application praying for amending the plaint. Since whereabouts of the learned Advocate for the defendant opposite party is not known, the learned Advocate for the petitioner could not serve any copy of the said application on the learned Advocate of the opposite party but nevertheless he sent a copy .of the same to the opposite party at their official address. To fortify his argument he relies on a decision reported in 29 D.L.R. 314 and sought to argue that even at a revisional stage an application for amendment of the plaint is entertain able and the court is competent to pass an order for amendment of the plaint. Mr. Hasan Foiz Siddique next submits that both the Courts below concurrently found that the plaintiff petitioner was dismissed from service without compliance of principle of natural justice and the same is violative of the rule 11 and 12 of the Jessore Board Rules and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside after allowing the prayer for amendment. He further emphasizes that since both the courts he low concurrently found on merit in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner, the relief should not be denied to him simply on a technical ground of absence of any prayer for consequential relief. He, however, in the course of his argument submitted that there is a prayer for back salaries but on a scrutiny of the plaint it is found that there is no such prayer in the plaint seeking hack salary from the date of dismissal from the service till reinstatement in the service. Mr. Hasan Foiz Siddique finally submits that if the resolution dated 5.11.85 goes, the subsequent conduct of the plaintiff petitioner cannot be a ground for his dismissal on the basis of the resolution dated 5.11.35. Supporting the findings of the trial court he further submitted that from the endorsement made by the appeal and arbitration committee of the Board in Exhibit A(10) it is clear that if the conduct of the plaintiff petitioner is not found to be satisfactory during the observation period a fresh disciplinary proceeding has to be initiated by the school authority in order to get rid of him but admittedly since that has not been done in the instant case the dismissal order is ex-facie illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 7. Before entering into the merit of the rule let me consider the application filed by the plaintiff-Petitioner for amendment of the plaint. On a perusal of the plaint it appears that the plaintiff made only 3 prayers in the plaint. The first prayer is to the effect that the resolution dated 5.11.85 adopted by the Managing Committee is collusive, fraudulent, void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff and the plaintiff is still in service. The second prayer of the plaintiff is to restrain the defendants from appointing anyone in the post of physical education teacher till the disposal of the suit and the 3rd prayer is for granting any other relief to which the plaintiff is entitled in law and equity. It thus appears that in the plaint there is no prayer for back salaries nor there is any prayer in the form of mandatory injunction for directing the opposite party to reinstate him in his former post. The evidence of P.W.1 was placed by Mr. Hasan Foiz Siddique and it appears that while he was examined as P.W.1 in support of this case he confined his examination-in-chief in terms of the plaintiff and he simply reiterated the prayer made in paragraph 'Ka' of the plaint. He neither claimed for any arrear salaries nor prayer for any mandatory injunction. On the contrary it appears from the written statement that in paragraph 3 it has been asserted by the defendant opposite party that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner and in paragraph 4 of the written statement it is further asserted that the suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. This written statement was filed before the trial court as back as 19.8.1989 and it appears from the record that the plaintiff respondent petitioner filed an application for amendment of the plaint on 19.2.90 but in that application no attempt was made by the plaintiff-petitioner to seek any amendment with regard to the relief namely for back salary and mandatory injunction. It further appears from ground No. 8 of the Memo of Appeal that it was specifically asserted by the defendant opposite party before the appellate court that the suit is not maintainable in law and during the course of hearing of that appeal it appears from the impugned judgment that the learned Advocate for the defendant appellant asserted that the suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, but till the pronouncement of the judgment by the appellate court no attempt was made by the plaintiff petitioner to amend their plaint to bring the suit within the ambit of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. No doubt, it has been held in the case reported in 29 D.L.R. 314, that Rules of procedure are intended to act in aid of administration of justice. A party cannot be refused a just and legitimate relief merely because of some mistake in the pleadings due to inadvertence. The courts have always acted in aid of and to further the cause of justice and not to deny or frustrate it. Once the court is satisfied that the party was acting bonafide and by his mistake or omission he has not caused any injury to the other side there is no reason why the court should refuse a legitimate and just prayer to amend the pleadings. It has been further observed by the learned Judge that the scope of interference by this court under section 25 of the Small Causes Courts Act is much wider than under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the scope of interference under section 115 is restricted. A question naturally arises in the instant case as to whether an application for amendment of the plaint in a revisional jurisdiction is entertain able or not. It is well settled that an appeal is a continuation of the suit but a revision is not a continuation of the suit. In an appeal there is a provision of counter objection but in a revision there is no provision for counter objection. When there is no scope for further appeal the order attains its finality and in a revisional application only on some limited ground i.e. on point of law only the court can interfere. In that view of the matter I am of the opinion that in the instant case there is no scope for entertaining an application for amendment of the plaint. Be that as it may, even if it is assumed for argument's sake that in an appropriate case by exercising it's inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure a court can pass an order of amendment even then in the instant case the prayer for amendment cannot be entertained as I have already found that the suit was filed on 25.11.1986 and the written statement was filed on 19.8.89 wherein the defendant had specifically raised this objection and-thereafter the plaintiff petitioner amended the plaint on. 9.2.1990 but for the reason best known to him he ultimately did not seek any amendment to overcome that objection. Not only that the plaintiff petitioner even at the stage of deposition did not assert that he is entitled to back salaries for the period from the date of his dismissal till the date of his reinstatement nor there was any prayer for mandatory injunction to make the declaratory decree executable. If the present application for amendment of the plaint is allowed that also would not serve the purpose and save the suit inasmuch as admittedly there is no prayer for back salaries which is another form of consequential relief in the instant case. In that view of the matter I am of the opinion that even on mitt the application for amendment of the plaint merits no consideration and the same must be rejected this legal aspect was brought to the notice of the plaintiff as back as 19.8.1989 and thereafter till today no attempt was made by the plaintiff petitioner to remedy the fault whereas in the meantime a right has accrued in favour of the defendant and this stand on the way of the plaintiff to get a prayer for amendment allowed. In that view of the matter this application for amendment of the plaint is rejected. The proposition laid down in the case reported in 29 D.L.R. 314, is not disputed and it is now well settled that the court must be liberal in allowing an application for amendment but as I have already held that in a revisional application there is no scope for amendment of the plaint, the case relied on by Mr. Hasan Foiz Siddique has no manner of application in the instant case as the said case was decided under section 25 of the Small Causes Court Act. 

 8. Now let me advert to the other points raised by Mr. Hasan Foiz Siddique in support of this rule. I have already mentioned in the forgoing paragraphs that the learned trial court conclusively found that in dismissing the plaintiff petitioner the defendant opposite party has failed to comply with the provisions of rules promulgated by the Board in 1979 as well as the dismissal order is violative of the principle of natural justice but it appears on perusal of the trial court's judgment that the trial court did not decree the suit on that count rather the learned trial court took the view that since the appeal and arbitration committee directed keeping plaintiff petitioner under observation for 6 months the dismissal order passed in pursuance of the resolution dated 5.11.85 lost its force and in order to dismiss the plaintiff from the service a fresh disciplinary action as to be initiated in pursuance of the rules of the Board and since the Managing Committee failed to do so, he decreed the suit. It also appears on a perusal of the impugned judgment that the learned appellate court below also concurred with that finding of the trial court but dismissed the suit on other points. The finding of the learned trial court that after the reinstatement of the plaintiff-petitioner in his service in pursuance of the directive of the appeal and arbitration committee the resolution dated 5.11.85 lost its force is erroneous and contrary to the evidence and materials on record inasmuch as the said findings of the trial court is based on the contents of the application that was made by the plaintiff petitioner in pursuance of directive of the appeal and arbitration committee but the learned trial court failed to take into consideration the directive given by the appeal and arbitration board wherein they have directed the school authority to place the plaintiff petitioner under supervision for 6 months and then to report about his performance. It also appears from the record that on 22.5.86 the plaintiff petitioner was asked by the defendant opposite party to attend the meeting held on that date but the plaintiff petitioner expressed his inability to attend the meeting on the ground of his illness. It also appears that in support of his illness he did not submit any medical certificate and the board in their meeting found that the excuse was a lame excuse without any basis whatsoever. Be that as it may, thereafter the Managing Committee resolved that the petitioner should go and accordingly sent their report to the appeal and arbitration committee. On receipt of the said report the committee again directed the plaintiff as well as the opposite party to appear before them and place their case and the appeal and arbitration board after hearing both the parties finally approved the proposal for dismissal and in pursuance of that order of the appeal and arbitration hoard the school authority ultimately dismissed the plaintiff petitioner from service. It is admitted by the plaintiff petitioner in his cross-examination that “বোর্ড কর্তৃপক্ষ ১৬/৭/৮৬ ইং তারিখে আমাদের উভয় পক্ষকে বোর্ড এ হাজিরা হওয়ার নির্দেশ দেয় এবং উক্ত তারিখে আমরা উভয় পক্ষ বোর্ডে হাজির হই এবং ঐদিন উভয় পক্ষকে শুনে বরখাস্ত আদেশ চুড়ান্ত ভাবে অনুমোদন করা হয়। বিভিন্ন সময়ে স্কুল কর্তৃপক্ষ ও বোর্ড কর্তৃপক্ষ আমাকে শুনানীর সুযোগ দিয়েছে।” 

 This endorsement does not indicate that after compliance of the direction given by the appeal and arbitration board, the Managing Committee has to initiate a fresh proceedings rather it indicates that if the performance of the plaintiff is not found to be satisfactory during the period of observation plaintiff could be dismissed on the basis of the charge already levelled. After the receipt of the report the appeal and arbitration committee again notified the plaintiff as well as the opposite party and asked them to appear before them and accordingly they appeared before appeal and arbitration committee and after full dress hearing given by the appeal and arbitration committee they finally approved the proposal of dismissal and in that view of the matter at no stretch of imagination it can be said that “ব্যবস্থা লওয়া যাইবে” means a fresh proceeding has to be initiated. I do not find any substance in his submission as well. I have already quoted the terms of the prayers made by the plaintiff petitioner in paragraph A of the prayer portion of the plaint which he reiterated in his deposition before the trial court and from that it appears that the instant suit has been filed only for simple declaration that the dismissal order passed by the Managing Committee in pursuance of the resolution dated 5.11.85 is fraudulent, void, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff and he is still in service. Such a prayer if not followed by any prayer for consequential relief in the form of back salary and for mandatory injunction to reinstate him in former post is hit by the proviso of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It has been held by a Single Bench of this Court in the case reported in 35 D.L.R. 225 that in a suit for declaration that plaintiffs dismissal was illegal and not binding without asking for consequential relief for enforcing the declaratory decree, omission to pray for consequential relief for enforcing declaratory decree renders it unenforceable in law. 

 11. It has been further held in that case the prayer for declaration was not followed by any consequential relief by way of any mandatory injunction and direction against the defendant to allow the plaintiff to continue in the service of the defendant and also by way of any claim for arrear wages and compensation. Omission to pray for any consequential relief for the purpose of enforcing a declaratory decree would be hit by the proviso of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Upon that ground the declaratory decree passed by the courts below becomes unenforceable which in turn would make the decree a nullity. 

 13. There is another decision to that effect reported in 15 B.L.D. 249, but unfortunately there is a Division Bench Judgment reported in 11 B.L.D. 528, wherein their Lordships dissented from the judgment reported in 35 D.L.R.'s case and held that a simple declaratory suit in a service matter without prayer for consequential relief is maintainable but in arriving at such a decision their Lordships of the Division Bench lost sight of the fact that the 35 D.L.R 's case was taken before the Appellate Division in the form of Special Leave to Appeal No. 229 of 1983 wherein their Lordships of the Appellate Division affirmed the judgment of the High Court Division observing that since the plaintiff's prayer for declaration was not followed by consequential relief the learned Judge committed no illegality in holding that omission to pray for any consequential relief for the purpose of enforcing the declaratory decree is hit by the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and by that judgment the legal position has been settled by the Appellate Division and there is no scope for this court to depart from that decision and in that view of the matter I must say that the decision reported in 11 B.L.D. 528, is a decision in per curium and not a binding precedent and that decision is not a good law so far that relates to the proposition that in a service matter a simple declaratory suit without a prayer for consequential relief is maintainable.
